notes: Idiomatic isBlockOpen/isBlockClose helpers fix the root cause across the dispenser and parser, and the parser tests plus a caddyfile_adapt integration test cover the exact issue scenario; it misses the quoted-address HasSuffix check, which is a minor edge.

Uses well-named helper methods applied consistently across dispenser and parser, but skips the quoted-token exemption for the address HasSuffix error and leaves the quoted "{}" new-line behaviour unchanged; it adds good parser tests and an integration adapt test that reproduces the issue.

Correctly adds a not-quoted check to every structural brace comparison in the dispenser and parser, including the address-suffix and quoted-'{}' cases, and has thorough dispenser and parser tests; it misses only the doImport anonymous-block key check, and the repeated inline checks are wordier than a helper.

Adds an unquoted-brace check at nearly every structural site, including the quoted "{}" fallthrough fix and the address HasSuffix check; it misses only the doImport anonymous-block check, and the repeated inline `&& !Quoted()` conditions are noisier than a helper, but the dispenser and parser tests are thorough.

Clean Token helper methods are applied at all the structural sites the reference touches, including the anonymous-block and address-suffix checks; it leaves the pre-existing quoted-'{}' branch unchanged, and its tests are adequate but less extensive.

Adds clean Token helpers used almost everywhere, including the address HasSuffix and anonymous-import checks; NextArg uses an inline check inconsistent with the helpers, the quoted "{}" branch is left as before (a quoted "{}" on a new line still merges into the previous directive), and tests cover the issue case.

The reported static-key case is fixed. But when either block's target is non-static, the new duplicate check treats a block in the same module as overridden, so a second `for_each` import block (or a static plus dynamic pair) on the same resource is still silently dropped. Precedence is decided only at the resource level and not after expansion, and the patch makes unneeded changes to the configs package and the transformer.

It fixes the reported static-key case, but treats any non-static import block in the same module (two for_each import blocks, or one static plus one for_each block on the same resource) as 'overridden' and drops it. It also drops a child's import entirely when the parent imports a single keyed module instance, and it adds unneeded changes to configs and transform_config, with only one basic test.

Returns all import statements and adds the same instance-level 'parent wins' check during expansion as the reference. The extra static pre-dedup is redundant but harmless. Tests cover static keys, `for_each` import blocks, mixed blocks, `count`, and parent precedence over an expanded child module.

Like the reference, it returns all statements and dedupes per instance during expansion so parent blocks still win. It adds a redundant but harmless static instance-level dedup, and its tests cover for_each, dynamic, mixed, count and expanded-module precedence.

Fixes the reported case and keeps dynamic blocks, but there is no expansion-time dedup. When the child module is expanded or a target is dynamic, a child block can overwrite the parent's import for the same instance, breaking the stated precedence. It also adds unrelated churn: a CHANGELOG entry, child sorting and a transformer rewrite.

It keeps all blocks and dedupes only static targets at config time, but has no dedup at expansion time. For expanded modules (or dynamic parent targets) the child's import overwrites the parent's, inverting the precedence, and it adds unrelated CHANGELOG, child-sorting and transform_config changes despite good test coverage.
